Backend.description: Which thing actually produced the verdict.

oneOf.description: The ACOS Rust runtime (VM, native loader, renderer, UI).
The legacy ACVM/AOSP reference backend.
Static host tooling (APK/DEX parsing, lint, build).
A host JVM used as a weak semantics oracle.
A physical Android device.

ErrorClass.description:
Who owns a failure: the app, the harness, the host, or a missing capability.

This is the classification the advisor's failure taxonomy requires (§10: `class ∈ {assertion, app_crash, unsupported, harness, infra_timeout, host_guard}`). It is derived from [`ErrorCode`] so a code can never serialize without a class.

oneOf.description: An assertion ran and did not hold (the app is wrong, or the expected evidence is wrong). Not retryable without changing the check.
The app crashed or stopped responding.
The engine/host cannot provide the required capability. Never a pass; choose another route or report it.
The harness itself failed (parse/serialization/protocol/invariant bug), or a failure that needs triage before it can be attributed.
A wall/CPU/log wait deadline elapsed.
A host resource guard fired (disk, memory, RAM guard, declared budget).

ErrorCode.description:
A stable, machine-readable ACOS error code.

The serde representation is the exact `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` string that agents branch on. Codes are additive: a code is never renamed or re-used for a different meaning.

An assertion ran and did not hold.
A selector matched no node.

A selector matched only nodes that are **not visible to the user** (for example a warm-mounted pager page parked off screen, or a node clipped away by an ancestor). The node exists in the tree but the user cannot see it, so it is never a pass for `wait_for`/`assert_text`/`assert_visible`/ `tap`; the error names the off-screen match and its bounds.

A selector matched **several** user-visible nodes and the caller did not say which one it meant.

Input and assertion verbs on the live channel refuse a silent pick: the error's `details.candidates` (`id`, `text`, `content_desc`, `class`, `bounds`) plus `details.selector` say exactly what matched, so the caller can pass a narrower selector (`id`, `content_desc`, `bounds`) or `index`.
A selector matched nothing in a tree the probe reported as truncated (`UiTree::truncated`, any window). The node may exist beyond the sampled prefix, so this is not proof of absence.
A UI node reference is no longer valid.
A tree-only assertion ran on an untrusted APK run, where the tree is guest-asserted and cannot corroborate a pass (fail closed).
The requested assertion kind has no implementation in this build.
The requested session does not exist (or was already destroyed).
The session is busy with another request.
The requested isolation level is not implemented for this app.
The process could not enter its confinement sandbox; native code is refused (fail closed).
The Landlock filesystem layer could not be assembled or proven on a kernel that supports it (fail closed). Distinct from `SECCOMP_UNAVAILABLE`.
The requested isolation level is advertised but its guarantees are unmet.
A memory admission/guard rule was triggered.
Execution was aborted by the RAM guard.
The operation exceeded its wall/CPU budget.
A declared resource budget was exhausted.
An untrusted APK run was requested while the product path is not certified for untrusted APKs. Only the labelled test override may run it.
The scenario is structurally or semantically invalid.
A request argument is invalid.
An artifact path was rejected (escape, absolute path, symlink, ...).
A native-library entry name attempts to escape its target directory.
The artifacts directory is incomplete or contradicts its verdict.
A render handle is invalid or already released.
A required font could not be found.
A renderer argument is invalid.
A render surface has invalid dimensions.
An image could not be decoded.
Renderer I/O failed.
Strict rendering mode escalated an otherwise-recordable fidelity loss.
The host scratch filesystem refused a write (ENOSPC/EDQUOT) or has less free space than the configured minimum. A host condition, never app behaviour; retrying after freeing space is safe.
The launcher (or another ACOS harness process) panicked. A harness bug: the panic message and the stage are evidence, not an app failure.
A host memory ceiling (launcher watchdog, cgroup limit, memcg OOM) was hit. Reduce concurrency or run on a host with more headroom; retry is safe once memory is available.

The host does not have room for another ART session right now: admitting it would drop `MemAvailable` below 10% of `MemTotal`. Distinct from `HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT` (a ceiling that was hit *during* a run): nothing ran. Class `host_guard`, retryable; `error.details` carries the measured MemAvailable/MemTotal and the session's memory budget.

The guest seccomp filter (and its proof) could not be installed. The host kernel/configuration cannot provide the isolation layer, so guest code is refused (fail closed). Distinct from `LANDLOCK_UNAVAILABLE`.
The guest process ended before the requested lifecycle stage completed. Carries the guest exit code, terminating signal and stage; inspect them to separate an app crash from a host condition.

The persistent zygote keeper (`ACOS_ART_ZYGOTE=on`) is gone or stopped acking a verb. The session is not served from the exec path while it reports zygote isolation: the reply names the keeper's exit status and the last zygote log lines, and the session is closed fail-closed.

The session daemon answered (or refused to identify itself) from a **different build** than the caller: crate version, build id (git sha + source digest) or the binary at the same path differ. The client never mixes builds — it replaces an idle auto-started daemon or runs its own private one; `error.details` carries both identities. Never retry against the same daemon; never read its answer as this build's behaviour.
ACOS itself failed (distinct from an app crash).

Evidence.description: Paths to evidence that backs this response.

screenshot.description: Fresh screenshot path (relative to the artifacts directory).

Fidelity.description:
How faithful the execution behind a result is.

* `static-analysis` — host parsing only. Proves nothing about runtime behaviour. * `jvm-reference` — host OpenJDK. Proves pure-Java semantics only; never Android/ART/framework/JNI/rendering behaviour. * `native-runtime` — executed by ACOS itself (its Rust VM/loader/renderer). This is **not** validated against ART unless `validated_against` says so. * `art-reference` — real ART on a reference Android image. Authoritative for Android framework behaviour at the stated API/ABI. * `physical-device` — a real device/OEM target. * `simulated` — a mock/stub path. A simulated success is not an Android success. * `n/a` — a **meta** reply: a tool that reports on ACOS itself (`acos_help`, `acos_capabilities`, `acos_doctor`). It says nothing about app behaviour, so labelling it `static-analysis` would imply the reply was derived from the APK. `n/a` never satisfies a fidelity requirement and is never a pass.

oneOf.description: Static host analysis only.
Host JVM (weak oracle; never Android-verified).

Physical device/OEM target.

Not applicable: a meta reply about ACOS itself (help/capabilities/doctor).

FrameMeta.description:
Metadata for one produced frame.

A frame answers a *cause* (the request/action id that produced it) and has a monotonically increasing per-session `frame_seq`. `content_hash` is the SHA-256 of the encoded pixels. `meaningful` is false for blank/placeholder frames; a placeholder must never satisfy a UI assertion.

cause_id.description: The request id that caused this frame (for example `req_19`).

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the encoded frame pixels (lowercase hex).

density.description: Display density in dots per inch.

display_origin.description:
Display-space coordinates of this frame's pixel `(0,0)`.

Absent means the frame covers the whole display and `(0,0)` is display `(0,0)` (the AOSP `screencap` case). A present value is authoritative: an agent must add it to convert a frame pixel into display coordinates, and subtract it for the reverse.

display_size.description: Full display size in pixels — the space `display_origin` and every UI tree bound are expressed in.

meaningful.description: True only when the frame reflects real rendered UI content.

produced_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp when the frame was produced by ACOS.

IsolationLevel.description:
How independent a session is from other sessions.

The levels are ordered from cheapest/weakest to strongest. A claim of data independence is only allowed at `sandbox` and above, and only when the engine actually implements the guarantees (see `docs/AGENT_API.md`).

oneOf.description: Another activity/task in a shared process and shared app data. No isolation.
Separate process, potentially the same package/storage identity.
Separate process/UID/credentials/mount namespace and app data.
Fully separate engine instance (strongest short of a VM).
Sandboxed full Android/backend for untrusted or device-level fidelity.

Metrics.description:
Wall/CPU/VM metrics for one request.

All fields are optional except `wall_ms`; the extra fields make the same object compatible with the existing `run-dex` metrics.

cpu_ms.description: Process CPU time in milliseconds, when measured.

peak_rss_bytes.description: Peak resident set size in bytes, when measured.

ProtocolError.description:
A structured error: stable code, human message, next action, retryability, and the failure class derived from the code.

Deserialization fills `hint`, `retryable` and `class` from the code when a producer omitted them, so an older envelope can never decode to a code with the wrong owner.

class.description: Who owns the failure (app, harness, host, unsupported capability). Derived from `code` on construction and on deserialization.

hint.description: What the agent should do next. Filled from [`ErrorCode::hint`] by default.

message.description: Human-readable detail (may change; never branch on it).

retryable.description: Whether retrying the same request without changing inputs may succeed.

Status.description:
The outcome of a request.

`unsupported`, `blocked`, `crash` and `timeout` are failures. An agent must never treat any of them as a pass.

oneOf.description: The request ran and every requested check held under the stated fidelity.
The request ran and a correctness check or assertion did not hold.
The harness, engine or input failed; not an app verdict.
The engine cannot perform the requested behaviour (never a pass).
The app crashed.
The request exceeded a wall/CPU budget or the app is not responding.
The request cannot start until an external condition is resolved (resource guard, busy session, unavailable isolation).

description:
The one JSON object every command returns inside `result`.

Fields are private so that `ok`, `status` and `error` cannot drift out of sync after construction. Use the getters and builders.
